english: Snell looks ahead the queue.
This'll take a while.
You sure you're done looking around?
I'd recommend we report to Lady Sageleaf before getting in line, but...
There's a heavy sound in his voice as he speaks to you.
His voice is strange. Deep.
If you feel like you're done.
He's going to miss this.
The goblin is very much okay going through a few more conversations with random people.
Before you do the deed.
It's been one hell of a quest.
A challenge for any mortal. But not for you.
Another job in the bag!
Hells yeah.
The time has come.
The END is NEAR.
Yeah. I don't feel like talking to more people. Let's wait in line.
(Wait until 12:00.)
E-No. I've still got stuff to do. (Leave and check around a bit more.)
Right. I'll probably go run some errands in the meanwhile. But go for it.
That stereotype about humans loving to queue... it's actually true, eh?
Time passes...
So slowly.
E-So slowly indeed.
A few people remain in the queue.
Though most are finished- done with this charade.
It's getting late.
We really should report to Lady Sageleaf right away. But beyond that...
Your companion looks around the chamber, the faint yellow light filling every corner.
Light into darkness. On the Day of Suffrage.
Might be time to cast your vote, eh?
The goblin gives you a tired smile.
Yeah. I've talked to enough people. Let's wait in line. (Finally vote in the election and finish up your quest.)
E-"Not yet." (Leave and check around a bit more.)
Only one dwarf left.
An indecisive fellow.
I wonder how long he's been standing here.
Hours?
Maybe he likes it. The anticipation.
I sure hope not, but... probably feels like it, yeah.
I guess if you're really that into voting...
Hey, wait- I think I saw him a while back. Has he been going in and out of the queue?
Crazy.
He clears his throat. "Anyhow."
(Yell at the dwarf in front.) "Hey, you having trouble making a decision? Wanna talk about it?!"
Oh yes. I've spent enough time here now. Let's vote before they close up. (Finally vote in the election and finish up your quest.)
E-"Not... yet." (Leave and check around a bit more.)
The dwarf turns around.
<shake>It's not easy, okay</shake>?!
Give me a minute!
He turns back to the ballot box, his shaking hand holding a crumpled voting card.
Relatable.
Give him time. And space.
What a farce.
In the far back you hear a goblin shush you loudly.
Snell is desperately stifling a fit of laughter.
You know what- why have a filter? Why not just say whatever comes to mind?
Who cares what the world thinks?
I might be a bit out of touch in everything social-cue related.
Wise words, Snell. Wise words.
Did I do something wrong?
The goblin lets out a long, drawn-out breath.
I must be getting acclimatized.
Well.
That's it then.
A bit of a wait, and then it's... done.
Exhaustion.
His words DRIP in it.
Nothing's ever truly done.
This vote is just the beginning, you know.
Quest complete.
Finally. I need a long-long rest.
That's true. There's still the...
He lets out a deep, disgusted groan.
So much paperwork.
Yeah. That's the scary part.
Bet you're real happy about that, you adventure-junkie.
Same.
Snell grabs one of the fence-poles nearby, leaning his body weight upon it.
How you holding up, by the way? We've been moving constantly, every waking hour, for... a long time now.
To just stand still like this... geezus, I feel like I'm getting feebleminded.
Gotta keep moving, man.
Without that chase, you might as well be dead.
There is still strength in these here bones.
A little... bit... LONGER.
Mm. Not sure how to even comprehend this damn day.
I'm still a bit in shock, I think.
It's work. Work work.
I'm a man. Men don't compress. They only expand.
Work work?
Work work.
The only true constant force of the universe.
He holds out two claws to signify the size.
An expanding manhood.
(Gesture alongside him.) "Massive."
Snell rubs his bloodshot eyes.
You could always talk to the press.
The press?
Yeah. Like, get this all down on print.
Great idea.
People will LOVE you.
That could be a wonderful opportunity to share some Azgalist love.
A man does not need his story to be told.
The larger the tale is when you fall into your grave, the bigger your manhood.
I got a friend at the Post who'd love to write about all of this. Lumiere Kolachov. She's this crazy lizard-woman. I think you'd like her.
Hey, you've read her work!
You have indeed.
She is a hack fraud.
Not sure how much you're able to say without getting in trouble with your bosses, of course.
Love her work.
Kolachov? She's a hack fraud.
You've got friends everywhere it seems.
I don't think I should talk to the press.
Could be fun. Maybe.
I don't care what Patriarchs think. They'll be out of a job after the election anyhow.
She's a - what do you say - special gal.
The type of 'acting' journalist, who writes inane, un-sellable, dialog-focused genre fiction on the side.
Absolutely. Just your type.
It's this line of work. I never seem to make acquaintances. Only enemies or friends.
He shakes his head.
Yeah. No, you're right. Too messy. It'd either be a scandal or a joke.
Something to think about.
I don't think even the Freestriders have the power to flip that entire hierarchy on its head. Not in years, at least.
I do like your thinking, though.
But that's for tomorrow. Or next week. Or next month.
Who knows how the city will look by then.
It will be a great SEISMIC shift.
Finally!
We'll get some golden glory going around here.
How hollow it all will feel afterwards.
But more importantly, will Snell be okay? Will his people make it through this change?
You will be lost in the aftermath.
Your SOUL lingering the ruins...
Will Lady Sageleaf be okay?
Will you be alright?
What do you think will happen to me after all of this?
Heh. Yeah.
Don't worry about her.
I'll be fine.
A nonchalant shrug.
With a hint of uncertainty.
I've helped build one hell of an institution here.
It'll make it through. No matter who's running the show.
The HWBT will survive. I'm sure of that.
Like hardy insects!
Whatever you do- do NOT equate them to cockroaches.
Unless you hit the timing just right, in which case... go for it.
(Nod.) "Like cockroaches."
I think you're right. You've got some spunk in you.
Time will tell.
No.
Hah!
Yeah. Like a bunch of fucking cockroaches.
We get stomped on, chewed on, spit out again...
Murdered en masse by some human god.
The goblin pauses for a moment in his rant, as if tasting the words.
Thriving in chaos.
Built some good shit, despite the odds.
Also forcibly assimilated.
Something like that, yeah.
Yeah. Fuck the odds.
Odds be fucked.
Fuck em!
They- it do- it do be like that.
That too, yeah.
...Sure.
We've got spunk.
It sure will.
No?
If the city falls, your kind will fall as well.
Norvik will outlive the Halfways. It's so much better.
Eh.
Maybe in this form. This Urthfolk-ish shape we're in now.
But if humans being adaptable is one of those traits of yours, then goblins are damn near polymorphic.
Keep that in mind, Cleric.
Yeah, yeah. And my dad could beat up your dad.
My father is dead.
Your father must be very powerful then.
He- oh.
Right. You told Ever-Glad about that.
It's okay. I got over it.
I don't think I'll ever get over it.
I never really got to know him.
Good job. Difficult thing to do.
Same, honestly.
Huh.
No clue, really.
My dad died a couple of years ago.
Oh.
Didn't know him too well. He was a syndicate-gob.
Like most in his generation, he wasn't too keen on anything human. Including this city.
So yeah. A bit complicated.
He was like most goblins then.
Yeah. Complicated.
Still. Sucks.
Of the last generation, sure.
Things are different now. We have actual opportunities. So I try not to judge.
Yeah.
Always does.
But you know what they say. The son doesn't have to... keep digging the trench, or whatever.
Just do your own thing.
Damn right.
We don't have to keep digging, but it's good to keep track of the trench. So we don't fall back in.
The goblin grins.
Now, you, on the other hand...
What about me?
Well...
What's your plan?
You will be the hero this city needs. No matter the cost.
You will serve. Bend over. Pray for mercy...
You'll make a fortune. Just gotta keep working.
If you're lucky you might have enough to eat next week.
You. Will. LIVE.
You. Will. DIE.
You will be the most powerful spellcaster on the Coast. In time, of course.
If they kick you out of the Towers, then you will surely start a coup.
You will help make this city a utopia for all.
Everything will be fine. The world is calm and lovely.
You'll be everyone's favorite person.
Eh.
You'll figure it out as you go along. That'll work great.
Uh...
Snell gives you a moment to think.
He's actually interested.
I'll be the best cleric I can.
I'll survive, somehow.
I'll hone my magic. Become even more powerful.
I'll find another job, if this whole cleric thing doesn't work out.
Yeah. I'm still thinking about it.
(Stay silent.)
Heh.
He shoots you a wicked grin.
I'm sure you already are.
Oh, that I'm sure of.
Honestly, not a bad idea. You're clearly a bit of an eso-maniac.
Well. I'm sure you've got connections.
He shrugs.
Your goblin companion stands there, waiting for an answer that doesn't come.
I get it. It's complicated. Still thinking about it, huh?
Thanks again for telling Darrow to shove it.
That was great to see.
I did? When?
You know. When he told you to 'dismiss' me.
That was cool. Really, didn't expect it.
I should also thank you for the, uh... resurrection.
I've never died before. Wasn't a great experience.
But I gotta say, if I'm ever gonna have to kick the bucket again- I'd prefer to do it next to you.
I would not choose you.
Same to you, Snell.
Figuratively.
Fair. Don't think I would be able to rezz you.
Apart from some basic heart massage, I guess.
Of course not. I'm The Cleric here after all.
Heart massage sounds nice though.
We'll have to change that. Get you some divine magic.
You sure are.
Nah. It's pretty violent, actually.
Bad choice. I don't have any god-channeled powers.
That's true. I retract my statement.
More exciting that way.
Maybe one day.
Smart move.
True. You're such a thrill seeker.
Oh yes. Snell the Cleric. Of which god?
Urth, of course.
Tokig the Gambler.
Illym could be fun.
I don't think they've got those helms in my size, sadly.
That would be insane. I like it.
We have different views on fun, I think.
Oh, and by the way...
Your voice is still really high.
What?
Since you downed that mirror potion. It's still high-pitched.
Shit. How long do you think it'll last?
High in a manly way, or...?
It sounds deep and stoic in my helm.
Give it a few more days.
Beyond that, I'm sure a faulty potion like that won't be hard to dispel.
Oh yes.
The manliest mouse in the kingdom.
Hm.
Reverb. Maybe.
The most evil grin you've ever seen. In your entire life.
Damn. What a heel turn.
It is, to be fair, absolutely hilarious.
...And I just realized we never actually went inside the tea shop.
...Huh.
We should have done that.
We really should have done that. I can't believe I forgot.
We did a bunch of other stuff?
We did.
But not the tea shop.
We did not, no.
Never made it inside. Huh.
I'm not sure how I'll explain that to Lady Sageleaf, but...
Eh, whatever. Mystery's solved either way.
As you keep talking, the chamber appears to grow ever-thinner in folk.
You only have a few more minutes left before it is time.
Now - before you head up - ask him!
Ask him what he's voting for! That'll help you figure him out for real!
The goblin sighs.
(Clear your throat.)
Yeah?
Hit me.
(Say it with a rough voice.) "What are you voting in the election, citizen?"
Eh, that's private.
Ugh.
He wants to have a piece of it to himself.
He fears.
Understandable. You know I had to ask.
Not even a hint?
You have to tell me. It's the law.
Come on... after everything we've been through?
I did expect, yeah.
Not yet it isn't.
Still private.
But he lets out a hearty scoff.
I'll tell you this much though- it won't be for the Freestriders.
That's rude.
Good choice.
The Freestriders don't need your vote.
He laughs.
I'm not sure how healthy an anti-stance really is, but...
Oh, I know.
I'm sure they'll win in the end anyhow. They always seem to do just that.
Yeah. That's where I ended up.
And you're red, I assume?
You're green, I assume?
And you're voting for... yourself, I assume?
But you're not voting at all, I assume? Or...?
And you're a damn Freestrider still?
And you're voting for...? What, the Party of Norvik or something?
Precisely.
Probably.
No. Or, uh...
(Look at the ballot box.) "I'll decide when I get there."
Cool. I read your many comments correctly then.
Right. Well, you're pretty hard to read, when it comes to that stuff.
I share your hesitation.
Fair.
I don't think... that's how it works, Cleric.
But... you do you.
Hah. There you go again. Always avoiding politics in the most awkward way possible.
He brings out a yellow notepad.
I'm not the type to write stuff down, I swear.
But at some point I realized I should note down how often you make all of these political comments. It got pretty ridiculous at some point.
Snell suddenly begins rooting around in his pockets.
Shit, right.
But at some point I figured I should note down how often you made those ridiculous political statements.
But my notepad...
He stops searching his jacket. "Damn. Must've dropped it in the City Below or something."
Oh, right. I have it here. (Hand him back his notepad.)
That sucks. Maybe you'll find it some day, in the far future. (Keep his notepad.)
...What?
Snell accepts it with a suspicious squint.
You dropped it at some point. I kept it safe.
I stole it from you.
...Alright. Uh. Thanks.
Wait, when exactly?
I thought I lost it before I even ran into you.
I took it from your pocket outside the Goblin Garden. Before you took me to Sageleaf.
No shit? Huh.
Pure disbelief.
With a hint of pride, of course.
I'm officially awarding you the title of the second most kleptomaniac bastard on Tolstad.
I accept the title with pride.
I reject that title.
This guy named Smarter. Let's hope you never meet him.
Yeah. Smarter.
Let's hope you never have the unfortunate luck to run into him again.
I had a feeling you would, you devil-handed bastard.
Too bad.
He brings up the notepad with a grin.
Eh. I'll buy a new one.
Then he flips through it.
Here.
Snell shows you a page with some scribbled lines.
Not as bad as I thought. It's less than a dozen times.
Maybe I need to get more... politically engaged, or whatever.
It's not worth it. Keep at your own pace, Snell.
You should. Each citizen needs to pick up their own weight.
Follow your heart, and whatever political policy burns a hole in the back of your skull.
Snell shows you a page of scribbled lines.
Oh yes. It's like, twenty times. That's bordering on obsession, you know?
Politics is everything.
We can always go harder. More political.
It's all about getting the foot in the door for the next Era.
Snell shows you a page FULL of scribbled lines.
It's like, thirty times, Cleric.
I'm not saying you shouldn't be politically engaged, but you're clearly a bit too fixated.
Politics is important. It's more important than all of us combined.
I breathe politics. It's in my veins.
Only thirty? I gotta pump those numbers up.
Politics is EVERYTHING and EVERYONE.
Never stop. Can't stop. (Start shaking.)
Snell shows you a page of many a question mark.
You're a bit of an enigma, Cleric.
An apolitical enigma.
Gotta stay mysterious. Keep 'em on their toes.
I suppose so.
The goblin shakes his head, placing the yellow notepad back into his jacket.
As he looks away, silence takes over between the two of you.
Ultimately, Snell breaks the silence with an almost stuttered sentence.
What did you, uh, if you don't mind me asking...
What did you talk about, with that guy? Urth, I mean.
Many things. He spoke about goblins. His role as a god.
Nothing I can tell you. (Leave him in the dark.)
He talked about goblins?
Yes.
About the...
What did he say?
He appeared as an old man with a lot of regret. Unsure about the many choices he made while alive.
He was a god. Stubborn and above it all.
He did his best in life. But he was unsure if that was anywhere close to enough.
It was an interesting experience.
I can only imagine.
Really?
Well. Never meet your heroes, and so on.
...Right.
I bet being a god is a pretty stressful position.
He did look pretty worn.
I bet being dead also does that to a guy. Anyway.
Thanks for telling me.
I'm sure... Lady Sageleaf will enjoy that in the report as well.
He did not ask for her.
Snell wanted to know- just for himself.
And he is happy to not have left those words unspoken.
How ominous.
But fine, I get it. We'll see if Lady Sageleaf demands more info later on.
There is something.
Hm?
Something is left unspoken.
It is weighing on Snell's mind.
Something... you can't quite put a finger on.
He takes a deep breath.
Just a bit longer. Then it's all done.
He does not want to address it. Unless you do it first.
But what is it?
Understand Snell.
(Ignore it.)
Snell is a good person.
He is a goblin.
Yet you have seen some great integrity within him.
That is not something you ever suspected in such a crossing.
You can trust him. And you understand him.
What's he thinking about then?
He is thinking of...
Urth.
Ah.
There is a lot unspoken about your encounter in the void.
Let him ask it.
You are thinking about something.
I am?
Yes, I can tell. Let's talk about Urth.
The goblin slowly closes his eyes, relaxing his posture.
He is carrying it no longer.
Yeah. I have to ask.
I just had a brisk conversation with the man who personally slaughtered my entire race.
Let me ask: what the fuck am I supposed to feel about that?
Rage and confusion.
I think you made your opinions very clear to his face. Which is impressive, by the way.
That is something you will only learn in time.
You may feel appreciation. He let you live.
I don't know, Snell. I am not a goblin.
Since you put it so concisely.
Snell lets his face fall into two palms.
Heh. I figured I'm the only goblin alive who's actually gonna get a chance to rage on the guy. Be a shame to let that chance slip away.
But...
He rubs his eyes.
Tsk.
In time. Like he's spouting some type of prophecy.
In the end, we'll all learn how correct he was, Snell says in a mocking tone. "Something like that."
He let my grandma live.
Everything else has just been...
And I am the only goblin alive, in the entire gods-be-damned world, that actually spoke with the bastard.
His brow furrows into scrunched mess as he adjusts his jacket.
A tic.
I don't know. Part of me hates that he got to me at all.
How do you mean?
He was pretty persuasive.
He just seems like a regretful old man.
I should've shot him with the sling for what he's done. But...
The goblin scoffs.
Exactly.
Something about that look in his eyes. I wouldn't expect that look in the eyes of someone with that kind of power. Who had that kind of power.

That he knew from the start... that it was all just a gamble. I don't know how to even process that. And that's how all those gods went about it? Following divine visions of whichever die roll had the greatest chance of success?
It's insane.
Yeah. Real world choices cannot be broken down like that. It's far too complex.
Sometimes I wonder if we all have our choices laid out like that. One after another. Just odds and Strings, in a tangled mess.
(Just let him speak.)
Agreed.
Yeah, no, that's... not something I've ever thought about. But I'm not exactly in-tune with the esoteric, so...
Snell places a claw up against his temple.
It's just- this old man stands there, defending every choice he's made. As if he were infallible- while also showing so much regret. Like he knows how much he's fucked up along the way.
But he'd still do it again!

Am I supposed to feel bad for him? Or should I be some all-forgiving monk, just because he did his best? On top of that- he has the gall to tell me what I should do? Like his words are anything other than the ramblings of a dead god?
Fuck. I don't know.
He looks down at the beautifully carved dwarven tiles.
...How do you feel about it?
